title: Matrices of nonnegative integer rank two
summary: The nonnegative integer rank of a matrix is a variant of the classical nonnegative rank, introduced in the 1980s, where factorizations are required to have integer entries. While computing nonnegative integer rank is generally very hard, we focus on a fundamental special case: determining when a rank 2 nonnegative integer matrix has nonnegative integer rank equal to 2 (the "rank2 problem"). Although this problem is trivial in the continuous case, in this context it is surprisingly rich.
